To restart:\n\n```bash\n# Docker Compose\ndocker compose restart\n\n# Docker Run\ndocker restart stirling-pdf\n```\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: HTTPS & Domain Setup\n\n> **🚫 Danger: Production Requirement**\n>\n> **Never run in production without HTTPS.** User credentials and PDF files will be transmitted in plain text over the network.\n\n\nUse HTTPS for access to Stirling PDF. You can terminate HTTPS at your existing reverse proxy or load balancer, or configure it directly in Stirling PDF.\n\n### Reverse proxy integration\n\n- Route requests to Stirling PDF's HTTP port (`8080` by default), using an address reachable from your proxy.\n- Preserve the public hostname and pass the original HTTPS scheme in `X-Forwarded-Proto`. If the upstream `Host` differs from the public hostname, also pass `X-Forwarded-Host`. These values are used when constructing login redirects.\n- Match the proxy's upload limit to the uploads you allow in Stirling PDF, and allow enough time for document processing.\n- For a subdirectory such as `/pdf`, set `SYSTEM_ROOTURIPATH=/pdf` and forward requests with that prefix intact.\n\nUse your proxy or hosting provider's documentation for certificate issuance, renewal and DNS setup.\n\n### HTTPS directly in Stirling PDF\n\nPlace your certificate keystore in the mounted `configs/` directory and configure `server.ssl` in `configs/custom_settings.yml`. Set `server.port` to the HTTPS port and publish that port in your container configuration.\n\nSee [SSL/TLS Configuration](doc:configuration/customisation/extra-settings) for the Stirling PDF settings and examples.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: User Management\n\n### 6.1: User Roles\n\n| Role | Can do |\n|---|---|\n| **Admin** | Use every enabled tool, manage users, change server settings, and view usage. |\n| **User** | Use the enabled tools and change their own preferences. |\n\n### 6.2: Adding Users\n\nOpen **Settings → Workspace → Users** and select **Invite people**. You can add several people at once.\n\n- **Invite by email** sends each person a link to join and set their own password. This needs [mail configured](#user-registration-control).\n- **Create account directly** sets a username and password for them. Share the password securely and turn on **Require a password change on first login**.\n\nChoose each person's role and team before sending.\n\n### 6.3: Managing Users\n\nFrom **Settings → Workspace → Users** you can reset a password, change a role, disable an account, or remove a member. Disabled users cannot sign in. Removing a member cannot be undone.\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Monitoring & Usage Tracking\n\n### 7.1: Logs\n\n```bash\n# Docker Compose\ndocker compose logs -f stirling-pdf\n\n# Docker Run\ndocker logs -f stirling-pdf\n\n# Last 100 lines\ndocker logs --tail 100 stirling-pdf\n\n# Errors only\ndocker logs stirling-pdf 2>&1 | grep ERROR\n```\n\nLook for errors, repeated warnings about disk space or memory, and failed sign-in attempts.\n\nTo limit log size, or forward logs to a collector such as the ELK Stack, Splunk, Graylog, or Datadog, configure a Docker logging driver:\n\n```yaml\nservices:\n stirling-pdf:\n logging:\n driver: \"json-file\" # local rotation; does not forward\n options:\n max-size: \"10m\"\n max-file: \"3\"\n```\n\n```yaml\nservices:\n stirling-pdf:\n logging:\n driver: syslog\n options:\n syslog-address: \"tcp://your-syslog-server:514\"\n```\n\n### 7.2: Health Checks\n\n`/api/v1/info/status` is always reachable without signing in. Use it for load balancer health checks and uptime monitors such as Uptime Robot or Pingdom:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/info/status\n```\n\nRequest counts are available at `/api/v1/info/requests/all` and `/api/v1/info/requests/all/unique`. They need a signed-in user or an API key, and `metrics.enabled: true` (the default).\n\nAlso watch disk space for the data directories:\n\n```bash\ndf -h\ndu -sh ./stirling-data/*\ndocker stats stirling-pdf\n```\n\n### 7.3: Prometheus (Team / Enterprise)\n\nTeam and Enterprise licenses include a Prometheus endpoint with HTTP request counts, grouped by endpoint, request method, and session. See [Usage Monitoring](doc:configuration/automation/usage-monitoring) for setup.\n\n---\n\n## Step 8: Backup & Disaster Recovery\n\n### 8.1: What to Backup\n\n| Data | Location | Frequency | Importance |\n|------|----------|-----------|------------|\n| **User database (if local)** | `./stirling-data/configs/stirling-pdf-DB-.mv.db` | Daily | Critical |\n| **Settings file** | `./stirling-data/configs/settings.yml` | After changes | Critical |\n| **Custom files** | `./stirling-data/customFiles/` | After changes | High |\n| **OCR languages** | `./stirling-data/tessdata/` | Weekly | Medium |\n| **Logs** | `./stirling-data/logs/` | Optional | Low |\n\nWithout an external database, Stirling PDF stores users in a local H2 file named `stirling-pdf-DB-.mv.db`, for example `stirling-pdf-DB-2.3.232.mv.db`. The simplest backup is the whole `configs/` directory.\n\n> **💡 Tip: Team/Enterprise Recommendation**\n>\n> Team and Enterprise deployments should use an [external PostgreSQL database](doc:configuration/storage/external-database) instead of the local H2 file, and back it up with your usual database tooling.\n\n\n---\n\n## Step 9: Performance Optimization\n\nFor resource sizing recommendations, scaling guidance, and fine tuning, see the dedicated [Performance Optimization & Sizing](doc:configuration/operations/performance-optimization) guide.\n\n---\n\n## Step 10: Paid Plans (Team/Enterprise)\n\nTeam and Enterprise plans add features for organizations, including:\n\n- **SAML 2.0 single sign-on** (Enterprise), with providers such as Okta and Azure AD.\n- **External PostgreSQL database** for reliability and scale.\n- **Prometheus metrics** and **Usage Analytics** under **Settings → Monitoring**.\n\nSee [Paid Offerings](doc:paid-offerings) for the full comparison, [pricing](https://stirling.com/pricing), or email support@stirlingpdf.com.\n\n---\n\n## Step 11: Optional - Document Automation & AI\n\n### 11.1: Stirling Processor\n\nSign in through a web browser and select **Processor** in the quick access bar on the left. It is not currently accessible from the desktop app, although we will be adding it for desktop apps connected to supported environments. Administrators and team leaders have access by default. Default users or environments without login will not be able to access Processor. Allow server folders before creating a folder workflow.\n\nFollow [Setup and access](doc:processor/setup-and-access), then [Create your first pipeline](doc:processor/getting-started).\n\n### 11.2: AI Features\n\nAI is off by default. Choose where it runs under **Settings → Server → AI Engine**:\n\n- **Run your own engine:** host the AI engine on an internal network with your own model providers. Follow [Self-Hosting the AI Engine](doc:ai/self-hosting-the-ai-engine).\n- **Use Stirling Cloud AI:** no engine or provider keys; the work runs on Stirling Cloud and is billed to the linked account. Follow [Stirling Cloud AI](doc:ai/stirling-cloud-ai).\n\nSee [AI Overview](doc:ai/ai-overview) for the available features.\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Steps\n\n- **Learn Stirling PDF:** the [Getting Started Guide](doc:getting-started) and the [Tool Reference](doc:functionality/functionality).\n- **Configure further:** [OCR languages](doc:configuration/operations/ocr), [Pipeline Automation](doc:configuration/automation/pipeline), the [API](doc:api), and [LibreOffice Parallel Processing](doc:configuration/operations/libreoffice-parallel-processing).\n- **Harden security:** [Fail2Ban](doc:configuration/security/fail2ban), an [External Database](doc:configuration/storage/external-database), and [System and Security](doc:configuration/security/system-and-security) settings.\n- **Keep it running:** test restoring your backups, and watch logs, disk space, and performance.\n\n## Resources\n\n- **Documentation:** https://docs.stirlingpdf.com\n- **GitHub:** https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF\n- **Issue Tracker:** https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/issues\n- **Release Notes:** https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/releases\n- **Discord:** https://discord.gg/HYmhKj45pU\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting Common Issues\n\n### Authentication Issues\n\n**Problem:** Can't log in as admin\n\n**Solutions:**\n1. ## Blocker

- **The spec says to reuse placement behavior without specifying the settings that make it meet the contract.** The existing `PdfUtils.addImageToDocument` uses landscape A4 only when `autoRotate` is true, and preserves aspect ratio only when `fitOption` is `"maintainAspectRatio"`; otherwise it can create portrait pages or stretch images. The existing image-to-PDF endpoint defaults to `autoRotate=false` and `"fillPage"`. See [PdfUtils.java](app/common/src/main/java/stirling/software/common/util/PdfUtils.java:535) and [ConvertImgPDFController.java](app/core/src/main/java/stirling/software/SPDF/controller/api/converters/ConvertImgPDFController.java:286). The spec should state that the dedicated workflow invokes placement with those required settings, or uses a helper that guarantees the specified A4 orientation and fit. This matters for both implementation and the tests in the verification section.

I found no other concrete architectural contradiction.
